task: We want to consolidate independent document-validation passes into a single AST walk and permit each pass to stop or skip work independently. Assess whether a straightforward shared visitor loop would preserve current behavior, especially when a pass edits a node. Find the top-level function declarations implementing the walk, visitor composition and handler selection, the type-aware wrapper, and executable-document plus SDL validation entry/implementation functions. Include overload signatures for those functions, but no nested callbacks, assertion convenience wrappers, classes or unrelated validators. Put these declaration locations in claims. In limitations, provide a source-cited behavioral compatibility assessment, explain the control signals and ordering, and describe the integration points and necessary regression checks. Do not infer runtime edges from declarations alone.

rubric.criterion: Distinguishes raw-walker BREAK terminating traversal from composed BREAK disabling only the individual visitor, on enter and leave. Other composed visitors continue.
reject: All visitors must return BREAK to continue

rubric.criterion: Explains per-visitor false-on-enter skipping state and resetting at the matching node leave, while other visitors can traverse the same subtree. false-on-leave is ignored for editing purposes.

First editing visitor returning null or a replacement short-circuits later visitors for that node in the corresponding phase. null removes, replacement may be traversed on enter. Does not claim every visitor sees the replacement.
reject: Every later visitor receives the replacement on the same enter

rubric.criterion: Describes ordered visitor dispatch, binding callback this to its own visitor, and node-kind-specific object/function handlers taking precedence over generic enter/leave handlers. A specific function supplies enter only.
reject: Specific function is both enter and leave

rubric.criterion: Explains type-info wrapper enters original node before callback, balances leave for any defined enter result, enters replacement AST node when applicable, and leaves node after leave callback. Explicitly preserves type-stack correctness around skip/edit.
reject: Every node always reaches ordinary leave callback

rubric.criterion: Identifies executable validation chain validate -> validateImpl -> composed rule visitors -> visitWithTypeInfo -> visit using QueryDocumentKeysToValidate. Mentions public tracing wrapper or schema/context creation where explaining integration.
reject: Executable validation uses only default traversal keys
validate directly loops over rules and invokes each full traversal

rubric.criterion: Identifies SDL path as SDLValidationContext and composed visitors passed directly to visit, without executable validation type-info wrapper. Distinguishes global validation abort/error-limit exceptions from per-rule BREAK.
reject: Per-visitor BREAK implements global maxErrors abort

rubric.criterion: Calls for regression checks spanning independent subtree skips, enter/leave BREAK, null/replacement order and visitor visibility, kind-specific/generic precedence, balanced type-info under edits, executable/SDL integration and global abort behavior. Rejects claiming declaration graph proves those behaviors. At least four distinct categories including skip/BREAK, edit ordering and type-info required.

corpus_selection: All production src/**/*.ts excluding __tests__, __benchmarks__, and __fuzz__ directories. No source file duplication. All actors receive identical full selected production tree.
independence: Authored from pinned TypeScript source by independent reviewer before reading analysis-tool output or evaluated-agent answers. Line numbers verified with nl and rg. No tool output used as oracle.
scoring: Each semantic point is 1 only when the answer establishes the essential proposition without contradiction and cites supporting source locations. 0.5 for correct but materially incomplete or uncited account. 0 for absent or wrong. Record exact answer excerpts and reasons. Structural exactness is independently scored from expected declarations.
limits: This tests change-impact reasoning assisted by declaration navigation. TreeSitterTool supplies declaration facts only. No call-graph or semantic-runtime inference should be attributed to it. Public known pilot, not hidden enterprise benchmark.
